body:
## Summary

Hive Mind now detects when a required Codex plugin is reported as installed or
available but its Agent Skills are not visible to the model. However, it does
not repair that state.

The preflight logs the missing skills, degrades to a warning, starts `codex
exec`, and the solver then stops on the repository's mandatory capability
preflight.

This issue is Codex-only. Claude plugin provisioning is out of scope.

## Confirmed reproduction

Target task:

- https://github.com/CEHR2005/GCS-TS/issues/3
- https://github.com/CEHR2005/GCS-TS/pull/4

Related Hive Mind work:

- #2074 / #2075 introduced repository-scoped capability provisioning.
- #2084 / #2086 added model-visible skill verification.
- PR #2086 explicitly deferred repair of `plugins/cache`.

Latest failing run:

https://gist.githubusercontent.com/konard/7bf6c48e206799c92357d623f9815b7c/raw/a4d35d12ceeca695a2a4f80bebad5578879b5c32/tmp-solution-draft-log-pr-1784536731842.txt.log.txt

Observed with `solve v2.8.7`:

```text
Codex capability preflight: detected 0 plugin and 6 skill requirement(s)
Verified superpowers@openai-curated in the Codex plugin catalog
Model-visible skills (5): imagegen, openai-docs, plugin-creator,
skill-creator, skill-installer
Codex capability preflight skipped: ... model cannot see:
superpowers:using-superpowers, ...
Continuing with the operator Codex capabilities.
```

Codex was then launched without the required skills and stopped without
implementation.

## Root cause

The repository-scoped `CODEX_HOME` can contain plugin configuration and a
marketplace snapshot without containing the materialized plugin payload under:

```text
CODEX_HOME/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/skills
```

Plugin catalog discovery or `installed/enabled` state is therefore not proof
that a skill is available to the model.

PR #2086 detects this condition through `codex debug prompt-input`, but
`prepareScopedCodexHome` still does not repair or reinstall the missing cache.
The failure is downgraded to a warning, so the expensive solver session starts
in a state already known to be unable to satisfy the task.

## Required behavior

For explicitly required Codex capabilities, before starting `codex exec`:

1. Create or refresh the repository-scoped `CODEX_HOME`.
2. Resolve the required skill provider from the trusted configured marketplace.
3. Materialize or repair the plugin payload in the scoped `plugins/cache`.
4. Probe the exact scoped environment using `codex debug prompt-input`.
5. Confirm every required skill is present in `<skills_instructions>`.
6. Start the solver only after that verification succeeds.
7. If repair or verification fails, stop before `codex exec` with an actionable
   diagnostic.

Requirements inferred heuristically from unrelated prose may remain advisory.
Requirements expressed explicitly as mandatory plugin/skill declarations must
fail closed.

`superpowers@openai-curated-remote` may be normalized to the Codex CLI
marketplace identifier `superpowers@openai-curated`. Satisfaction must be based
on the requested skills being model-visible, not on literal alias equality.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A regression test reproduces a scoped home where the provider is present
      in the marketplace/configuration but its `plugins/cache` payload is
      missing.
- [ ] The preflight repairs that state and materializes the plugin payload.
- [ ] `codex debug prompt-input` using the same scoped environment exposes all
      explicitly required `superpowers:*` skills.
- [ ] `codex exec` is never called before successful model-visible verification.
- [ ] An unrecoverable explicit requirement fails closed instead of logging
      `Continuing with the operator Codex capabilities`.
- [ ] Heuristic false positives can still degrade safely without blocking
      unrelated tasks.
- [ ] Provisioning is idempotent and persists across documented Hive Mind
      container restarts.
- [ ] Plugin state remains scoped to one repository and does not enable the
      plugin for unrelated repositories.
- [ ] The behavior works in direct Codex execution and Docker isolation.
- [ ] Tests cover stale cache, missing cache, successful repair, repair failure,
      alias normalization, repository isolation, and repeated execution.
- [ ] At least one end-to-end test uses a real Codex CLI and rendered prompt;
      mocked `plugin list` output alone is not sufficient.
- [ ] A rerun of CEHR2005/GCS-TS#3 reaches and invokes
      `superpowers:using-superpowers` instead of stopping at capability
      provisioning.

## Non-goals

- Claude plugin provisioning.
- Hardcoding a Superpowers-specific installation path.
- Weakening the mandatory workflow in CEHR2005/GCS-TS.
- Modifying or committing generated skills into the target repository.
- Adding another diagnostic-only layer without a repair path.

## Definition of done

The fix is complete only when a clean end-to-end rerun demonstrates that the
required skills are visible inside the actual solver session and the target
agent advances beyond its mandatory Superpowers preflight.
title: Codex capability preflight detects invisible required skills but does not repair repository-scoped plugin cache
